stem:
Indira starts with a square. She may build a new square on a diagonal of the given square, or join the midpoints of the given square's sides. She wants twice the area, and also half the area.

Which plan is correct?

options.text: Double the area by joining the midpoints; halve it by building on the diagonal.
Double the area by building a square on the diagonal; halve it by joining the midpoints of the sides.
Joining the midpoints doubles the area, and building on the diagonal also doubles the area.
Building on the diagonal halves the area, with no separate midpoint construction.

teacher.key_rationale: A square on the diagonal doubles the area; the midpoint-joined square halves it. Swapping those constructions reverses the relation. Claiming both constructions double omits the half-area role of the midpoint square.

mx_swap.reason: Inscribed-quadrilateral exclusion invents a figure family not named in the stem; kept relationship_reversal and condition_omission.
Squaring the diagonal as arithmetic invents an operation not in the stem; kept relationship_reversal and condition_omission.
